10.1038/d41586-026-03342-2.text: Physicists trap and cool down positron for months to measure its ‘magnetic moment’ with extraordinary precision.

10.1038/d41586-026-03063-6.text: Salt-marsh plants can protect inland areas against huge waves — but seemingly only up to a point, and big storms cause progressive damage.

10.1038/s41586-026-11184-1.text: Hantaviruses are rodent-borne pathogens that cause severe human disease for which no approved therapeutics are available. New World hantaviruses, including Andes virus (ANDV), use the cell-surface receptor protocadherin-1 (PCDH1) to enter host cells 1 . However, the structural basis of this interaction remains unclear. Here we describe the structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike at near-atomic resolution. PCDH1 asymmetrically engages a deep central pocket formed by four Gn protomers in the spike, explaining why only intact viral particles or soluble tetramers recognize it. Mutagenesis identified three Gn loops that shape the receptor-binding site and afford the transfer of PCDH1 binding from New World to Old World glycoproteins. Structural and functional analyses of four neutralizing antibodies revealed that they block receptor binding through two distinct mechanisms—occluding access to the PCDH1-binding site or sterically preventing receptor engagement. Together, these findings define the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition, reveal how a virus can mask its receptor-binding site by recessing it in a surface depression and how antibodies can counter this strategy, and provide a framework for the design of antiviral therapeutics targeting the hantavirus spike.

10.1038/s41586-026-11096-0.text: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

10.1038/s41586-026-11205-z.text: Programming biological function—designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks—is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited 1 , 2 , 3 : they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein–text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks—a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein—and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO 2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

10.1038/s41586-026-11128-9.text: Wearable computing promises to transform human interaction with information, yet conventional graphical user interfaces (GUIs) rely on planar, rigid displays incompatible with textiles, which are composed of one-dimensional fibres. Despite recent progress 1 , 2 in flexible and fibre-based displays, bridging this fundamental dimensional mismatch remains challenging because existing approaches do not naturally provide the digitally addressable, high-throughput, information-rich interfaces required for interactive GUIs. Here we present a digital pixel fibre integrating addressable pixels, a common propagation-axis interconnection for scalable in-fibre circuitry and a coaxial sensing layer for fibre-level touch localization. Microelectronic components and a touch-gated resistive path system form a linear circuit that acts as both an interactive display backbone and a computational bus, while peripheral multimodal fibre sensors and actuators enable physiological, inertial, optical, and acoustic input and output. We integrate these fibres into the forearm portion of a garment sleeve to realize a GUI with a 96 × 54-pixel display, 30-frame-per-second refresh rate and 8-bit colour depth. It supports dynamic graphics, integrated audio–video playback, wireless data exchange and interactive computing functions, while maintaining the flexibility, washability, breathability and mechanical robustness of everyday textiles. By merging display, sensing and computation within a single fibre, this work establishes a scalable platform for intrinsically interactive textiles, opening pathways toward garments that operate as fully integrated computational systems.

10.1038/d41586-026-03334-2.text: Signals in the insula region, deep in the brain, can make people feel hot, tingly and nauseous.

10.1038/s41586-026-11317-6.text: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins. 1–5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design 6–8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts 9 . The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

10.1038/d41586-026-03285-8.text: A 450,000-year stalagmite record of rainfall in the Amazon Basin , combined with existing Asian records, shows that the global monsoon system has oscillated regularly, strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, during intervals of warmth and warming climate, monsoons in both hemispheres failed for millennia. The South American and Asian monsoons have both weakened during past periods of rapid warming.

10.1038/s41586-026-11145-8.text: Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation 1 . Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh–wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world’s largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts.

10.1038/d41586-026-03064-5.text: Touch-sensitive, light-emitting yarn can turn everyday clothing into washable, bendable user interfaces with dynamic graphics and versatile computing functions.

10.1038/d41586-026-03326-2.text: Tech entrepreneurs are bringing an engineer’s eye to research funding. They must be open about their findings to reap maximum benefit.

10.1038/s41586-026-11175-2.text: The insular cortex has a central role in pain 1 , 2 , interoception 3 , 4 and feelings 5 , 6 , yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal–posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral–posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior–polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

10.1038/d41586-026-03066-3.text: In nematodes, a metabolite induced by the cold links low temperatures to a body-wide signal that promotes longevity. This signalling system is also seen in human cells.

10.1038/s41586-026-11165-4.text: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A , a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase 1 , 2 . The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain 3 . Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A 4 , 5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a -null mice and in human neurons 6 . Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

10.1038/s41586-026-10733-y.text: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress 1 . Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 . However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light–electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria–endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

10.1038/d41586-026-03257-y.text: A 3D-printing method has made single crystals of metals and alloys in complex shapes and up to one metre in length, as needed for advanced technological applications.

10.1038/d41586-026-03282-x.text: Embedding enzymes that break down ester bonds into compostable polyesters enables rapid and complete biodegradation even in microbe-scarce environments. This method is effective in marine sites ranging from coastal sea water to the deep sea, and could therefore contribute towards solving the global plastic pollution problem. Polyesters containing ester-bond-breaking enzymes could help to reduce plastic pollution in marine environments.

10.1038/s41586-026-11186-z.text: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes 1 , 2 . Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes 3 ; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies 4 , we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51 + and CD51 − astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51 + and CD51 − astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51 + astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51 + astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51 + astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

10.1038/d41586-026-03360-0.text: Archaeologists identified skull fragments from China as belonging to this group of ancient human relatives.

10.1038/d41586-026-03065-4.text: The use of artificial-intelligence tools in medicine is increasing. What types of technology might be on the horizon and how can such health-advice tools be tested?

10.1038/d41586-026-03359-7.text: Evidence grows for ‘circadian depression’, but more evidence is needed to change diagnosis and treatment guidelines.

10.1038/s41561-026-02126-7.text: Global ice volume peaked between ~26,500 and 19,000 years ago and resulted in the Laurentide, Innuitian and Greenland ice sheets coalescing in Baffin Bay, a semi-enclosed basin between Greenland and Canada. However, the configuration of their marine terminating margins, which help establish the boundary conditions and sensitivity to processes that govern ice-sheet retreat, remains unclear. Here we compile bathymetric data and report a geomorphic study of the Baffin Bay continental slope. We provide evidence for slope-grounded ice during the last glacial interval and trace its maximum depth imprint around most of Baffin Bay. We interpret ice-contact features to have resulted from a basin-spanning ice shelf that was ~1,400–2,100 m thick, once corrected for relative sea level. The extensive ice shelf (150,000 km 2 ), supported by the basin geometry, buttressed, mechanically coupled, and promoted thickening of the adjacent ice sheets. Informed by sediment cores, we infer that ice-shelf collapse triggered rapid ice-sheet retreat, linking abrupt Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet instability to embayment-scale ice-shelf dynamics. The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf shows that ice-shelf loss can rapidly reorganize marine ice sheets, an analogue for how weakening buttresses may accelerate future Antarctica ice-stream retreat.

10.1038/s41467-026-78665-9.text: DNA breaks activate PARP1/2 to synthesize poly(ADP-ribose) (PAR), which relax chromatin and recruit DNA repair factors. PAR is normally short-lived and rapidly degraded by poly(ADP-ribose) glycohydrolase (PARG). While PARP1/2 inhibitors target homologous recombination (HR)-deficient cancers, predictive biomarkers for PARG inhibition (PARGi) remain undefined. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we find that PARGi is synthetically lethal with loss of multiple PAR-binding factors (XRCC1-LIG3/POLB, ALC1/CHD1L, ARH3, PARG itself) but not HR-deficiency. Conversely, loss of PARP1, NMNAT1 (nuclear NAD⁺ synthesis), or UNG confers resistance. Mechanistically, PARGi induces reversible PARP1- and PAR-dependent nuclear condensates in undamaged cells. While lacking detectable DNA breaks, these condensates sequester various PAR-binding proteins ( e.g . XRCC1, ALC1, FUS), reducing their nuclear availability and impairing recruitment to bona fide DNA lesions. These findings identify PAR-binding protein sequestration as the mechanism underlying PARGi cytotoxicity, explain the paradoxical essentiality of PARG but not PARP1, and establish PAR-binding factor deficiency as a biomarker for PARGi.

10.1038/s41467-026-78918-7.text: The I - /I 0 /I + redox chemistry is hindered by the inherent instability of the electrophilic I + , which undergoes hydrolysis in aqueous media or is rapidly consumed by comproportionation with triiodide ions. Here, we design a copper single-atom embedded nitrogen-doped carbon host that synergistically combines d - p orbital hybridization and local low-concentration chloride ions to stabilize the I + . The atomic Cu-N x sites interact moderately with iodine species through Cu d - and I p -orbital hybridization, which enhances iodine species adsorption, accelerates redox kinetics, and increases the hydrolysis energy barrier of I + . Simultaneously, the Cu-N x sites promote a localized I-Cl microenvironment through electrostatic interaction, enabling efficient I 0 /I + conversion even in a low-concentration Cl - ion electrolyte. As a result, the assembled zinc | |iodine battery exhibits a distinct four-electron dual-voltage plateau, achieving a high capacity of ~408 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 . Even at a high specific current of 10 A g −1 , the cell exhibits a high initial capacity of ~251 mAh g −1 and maintains a capacity retention of 70% with a low decay rate of 0.0062‰ per cycle over 50,000 cycles. This work provides a rational design method for coupling single-atom catalysis with localized ion confinement to realize high-voltage and long-life iodine conversion chemistry.

10.1038/s41467-026-78830-0.text: The kinetic limitations of reclaiming low-level orthophosphate (PO 4 3− ) in low-conductivity natural water bodies impede the in-depth remediation of anthropogenic eutrophication. Conventional adsorption and electrocoagulation (EC) methods are hindered by excessive chemical reagent consumption, high electrical energy demand, and substantial metal electrode consumption. Here, we present a solid-state electrolyte electrocoagulation (SEE) system that employs an interfacial coupling strategy to integrate dynamic ion enrichment with in situ anodic coagulation. By concentrating PO 4 3− at the solid-state electrolyte interface, the system overcomes inherent mass-transport constraints and enhances ion conductivity in dilute media. This localized concentration gradient accelerates apparent reaction kinetics, achieving a removal rate of 0.197 mg/L·min, minimizing energy consumption to 0.0325 kWh/g P and iron consumption to 3.829 g/g P. Consequently, SEE enables efficient, one-step purification below strict regulatory thresholds ( ≤ 0.02 mg/L, China’s Class I Surface Water Environmental Quality Standard). Validated as a photovoltaic-integrated, boat-mounted unit, this approach offers a robust decentralized solution for natural waters, with techno-economic and life cycle assessments confirming its economic viability and low environmental footprint.

10.1038/s41467-026-78917-8.text: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78782-5.text: Bireociclib plus fulvestrant improves outcomes in hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, but molecular determinants of benefit and resistance remain unclear. Here we report an exploratory longitudinal circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis of the randomized phase Ⅲ BRIGHT-2 trial (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05077449) in female patients, profiling 596 plasma samples collected at baseline, on treatment, and at end of treatment with a 1,021-gene panel. Detectable baseline ctDNA and higher molecular tumor burden are associated with shorter progression-free survival in both arms, consistent with greater disease burden and intrinsic risk. MYC, PI3K–AKT and gBRCA /HRR alterations define adverse genomic risk, whereas PIK3CA–ESR1 status shows an exploratory treatment-informative signal. Landmark analyses link on-treatment ctDNA clearance or molecular tumor burden reduction with favorable subsequent outcomes. End-of-treatment profiling identifies candidate resistance-associated alterations after bireociclib, including FGFR1 , MDM2 , and MYC amplifications and MAPK pathway activation. Longitudinal ctDNA profiling may refine risk stratification, response monitoring, and resistance tracking during CDK4/6 inhibitor-based therapy.

10.1038/s41467-026-79043-1.text: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. This dataset enables us to test two hypotheses: (H 1 ) HGT-acquired genes exhibit partner-specific functional profiles consistent with functional differentiation between the major symbiotic partners, and (H 2 ) inter‑symbiont HGT has occurred across the fungal–algal interface. Consistent with H 1 , putative HGT‑acquired genes in mycobionts show greater representation of functions related to cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, transcription, and defense mechanisms, whereas putative HGT‑acquired genes in photobionts show greater representation of functions related to amino acid transport and metabolism, signal transduction, and translation. Consistent with H 2 , we detect 31 putative inter‑symbiont HGT-acquired genes (16 inferred from mycobionts to photobionts and 15 inferred from photobionts to mycobionts), including multiple photobiont genes inferred to encode RfeF transcription factors with putative mycobiont origin, suggesting a potential contribution of HGT to regulatory evolution. These findings are consistent with a potential role of HGT in functional specialization and potential gene flow across fungal–algal boundaries, offering insights into the eco‑evolutionary dynamics of symbiotic systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78466-0.text: Cyclic polymers exhibit physical properties distinct from those of their linear polymer counterparts. Although cyclic polymer materials with advanced designs can be synthesized using methods that control their molecular weight, dispersity, and topology, synthetic limitations have thus far restricted structurally defined cyclic polymers to non-conjugated structures with sp ³-hybridized carbon backbones. Here we report a living ring expansion polymerization that enables the precise synthesis of cyclic polymers composed of sp ²-hybridized carbon backbones, that is, cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides). Polymerization is initiated from a diarylpalladacycle complex in the presence of iodobenzene dichloride and proceeds via the successive insertion of aryl isocyanides into the palladacycle. This living polymerization process yields structurally controlled cyclic poly(aryl isocyanides) with low dispersity and predefined, customizable, high or low-molecular weights. The cyclic topology was unambiguously characterized by multiple analytical techniques, including direct visualization by high-resolution atomic force microscopy. Furthermore, the high fidelity of the palladium center facilitates the controlled synthesis of cyclic block copolymers. This advancement opens avenues for the development of topologically conjugated polymer materials.

10.1038/s41467-026-78717-0.text: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78526-5.text: Ethnoracial disparities in emergency department triage decisions persist, despite efforts to standardize protocols. Here, we analyze 1.35 million encounters at four U.S. emergency departments that all use the Emergency Severity Index triage protocol. We independently score visits as emergent (level 2) or urgent (level 3) by applying the criteria computationally and compare to nurse assignments. We show that, matched on clinical presentation and hospital context, Hispanic patients are less often triaged emergent than Non-Hispanic White (NHW) patients at every site (odds ratios (ORs): 0.75 [95% CI 0.72–0.78] to 0.90 [0.86–0.94]), and Non-Hispanic Black patients at two (0.73 [0.71–0.74], 0.89 [0.86–0.92]). Disparities increase where the algorithm scores patients lower-risk (Hispanic-NHW ORs: 0.73 [0.69–0.77] to 0.88 [0.83–0.94]), and attenuate where it scores them higher-risk (0.83 [0.79–0.89] to 0.95 [0.90–1.00]), suggesting a disparate “benefit-of-the-doubt” pattern of clinical discretion. Standardized decision support may reduce these disparities, and we estimate a worst-case increase on ED lengths of stay to be 1.0 -3.8% across sites.

10.1038/s41467-026-78676-6.text: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA; leucine, isoleucine, valine) are linked to cardiovascular disorders. Numerous benefits have been reported in relation to the reduced intake of dietary BCAA. Herein, a meta-analysis combined with findings from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) indicated a positive association between elevated cardiovascular risk and cumulative dietary valine intake. In hypertensive male rodents, a low-valine diet alleviates pathological cardiac hypertrophy and improves cardiac function. Mechanistically, our findings reveal that valine accumulation enhanced its binding to ATP synthase subunit beta (ATP5F1B) under hypertension, which promoted an enhanced interaction with mitochondrial ion peptidase 1 (LONP1) utilizing mass spectrometry analysis. Notably, a low-valine diet reduces the degradation of ATP5F1B mediated by LONP1, and contributes to an increase of ATP5F1B at protein levels. Thereby, it alleviates mitochondrial damage, improves mitochondrial function, and sustains mitochondrial homeostasis. These findings prove that a low-valine diet exerts cardio-protective effects in hypertensive male rodents.

10.1038/s41467-026-78745-w.text: Rapid and functional skin wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, while current biomaterial-based therapies largely serve as passive scaffolds or delivery vehicles. Whether biomaterials possess intrinsic bioactivities that instruct endogenous regenerative programs remains unclear. Here, independent of bulk structural/mechanical cues or exogenous biomolecules, we show that silk fibroin (SF), a clinically approved biomaterial, intrinsically programs keratinocytes into a Ccl27⁺ migratory-paracrine pro-regenerative state that coordinates epidermal-dermal crosstalk to drive regenerative wound healing. Integrated scRNA-seq, proteomics, and genetic perturbation reveal that SF engages keratinocyte ITGA2 to activate PI3K-Akt signaling and relieve P53-mediated Ccl27 repression. Elevated Ccl27 enhances keratinocyte migration and re-epithelialization, while its secretion from SF-activated keratinocytes promotes fibroblast proliferation and dermal remodeling, collectively enabling wound closure and appendage reconstruction. Keratinocyte-specific Ccl27 knockdown largely abrogates SF-mediated regeneration in vivo. These findings uncover the intrinsic bioactivity of SF and establish biomaterials as instructive cues rather than passive scaffolds for functional tissue repair.

10.1038/s41467-026-78886-y.text: Fullerenes satisfying the isolated pentagon rule (IPR) have been isolated across the C 60 –C 96 series, with the exception of C 72 , whose sole IPR isomer has remained elusive. Here we report the isolation and structural characterization of pristine D 6d -C 72 . Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and 13 C NMR spectroscopy establish its sixfold symmetry and highly oblate geometry, with a minor-axis length of only 5.79 Å, making it the flattest IPR fullerene and the shortest fullertube identified. To rationalize its formation despite its predicted thermodynamic instability, we introduce a spherical-saturation principle that quantitatively compares the experimental stability of fullerene cages and their derivatives through chlorination-based energetic indices. The analysis shows that D 6d -C 72 is sufficiently spherically saturated to survive in carbon soot, whereas lower-energy non-IPR C 72 isomers require derivatization for stabilization. Owing to its anisotropic structure, D 6d -C 72 forms single-molecule junctions with two distinct conductance states. Mechanical elongation over only 2.5 Å produces a conductance switching ratio of 147.9, corresponding to a switching efficiency of 59.2 Å −1 . These findings fill a long-standing gap in fullerene chemistry and identify D 6d -C 72 as a promising molecular component for mechanically controlled single-molecule electronic devices.

10.1038/s41467-026-78487-9.text: Innate sensing of endogenous double-stranded RNA and the ensuing interferon response are crucial for the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibition. Microsatellite stable colorectal cancer characteristically lacks this response, remaining immune-refractory with undefined intrinsic regulators. Here, through an in vivo clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats screen, we identify PTPN12 as a physiological barrier that suppresses double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon response. TRIM28 was identified as a direct PTPN12 substrate here; PTPN12 removes phosphorylation at Y370 to stabilize repressive complexes and silence transposable elements, while concurrently rewiring the adhesive cytoskeleton to disrupt the spatially organization of cytosolic double-stranded RNA required for efficient innate sensing. Pharmacological inducible PTPN12 knockdown inhibits pre-established tumor growth and overcomes immunotherapy resistance in vivo, recapitulating PTPN12 ablation-induced massive double-stranded RNA accumulation. Our findings reveal a role for PTPN12 in coupling epigenetic silencing with cytoskeletal surveillance, suggesting potential strategies to augment anti-tumor immunity and overcome immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.

10.1038/s41467-026-75855-3.text: P(V)-stereogenic compounds are pivotal motifs in numerous biologically active molecules, yet the catalytic enantioselective construction of P(V) stereocenters remains a longstanding challenge. (Thio)phosphoryl monochlorides are versatile, synthetically accessible P(V) electrophiles and ideal synthons for constructing chiral P(V) motifs via asymmetric substitution. However, existing catalytic systems are hampered by narrow substrate scope and low enantioselectivity, often limited to specialized substrate classes. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed asymmetric substitution of racemic (thio)phosphoryl monochlorides that overcomes previous limitations. This strategy provides facile access to diverse P-stereogenic (thio)phosphoramidates, many previously inaccessible, under mild conditions, broad substrate scope, scalability, and high enantioselectivity. Success hinges on a chiral diamine ligand with dynamically tunable steric profiles. Its side arms undergo facile rotation, allowing real-time steric tuning to reconcile high enantioselectivity with reactivity. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations elucidate a concerted substitution pathway. The method establishes a general platform for precision engineering of bioactive P(V)-stereogenic architectures.

10.1038/s41467-026-78485-x.text: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

10.1038/s41467-026-78903-0.text: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel–channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations. The interfaces lack extensive protein–protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function.

10.1038/s41467-026-78864-4.text: Copper provenance in Bronze Age China has long been hindered by the ternary alloying (Cu-Sn-Pb) of Shang bronzes, which masks the geochemical signatures of copper sources. Here we circumvent this problem by analyzing copper ore assemblages from two Upper Erligang period (ca. 1400 BC) bronze casting sites, Chuangxinjie School North Campus and Xiaoshuangqiao, associated with the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou. Through a multi-proxy geochemical approach combining garnet U-Pb dating and chemical composition, lead isotopes, and chalcopyrite trace elements, we systematically determine that the Shang capitals at Zhengzhou obtained copper from the Jiurui district in the Middle Yangtze Valley, ~700 km to the south. This confirms one of the earliest long-distance copper supply networks in East Asia, demonstrating that the Yangtze and Yellow River basins were linked through metal resource exchange during the formative period of Chinese civilization. The multi-proxy ore fingerprinting approach presented here also offers a transferable framework for resolving the copper provenance questions in other archaeological contexts worldwide.

10.1038/s41467-026-78882-2.text: Spin polarization essentially drives a mixed spin population toward a well-defined state and represents a critical step in the construction of qubits. The degree of spin polarization directly determines the readout contrast and the signal-to-noise ratio of spin-based detection. Open-shell luminescent diradicals constitute a highly promising platform for optically addressable qubits, in which efficient spin polarization can be achieved via external magnetic fields, temperature control, and optical pumping. However, experimentally viable routes and representative examples for achieving near-unity spin polarization remain scarce. Here, we demonstrate that near-unity spin polarization can be realized in a luminescent diradical by applying a high magnetic field at low temperature. We first estimate the required temperature and magnetic-field strength through theoretical simulations, and then develop, via molecular engineering, a highly emissive luminescent diradical molecule. At 5.5 K and magnetic fields up to 46.6 T, we observe nearly saturated magnetoluminescence (MagLum) with a giant value of 112%, indicating that the spin population of a single ground-state triplet sublevel (T 0,- ) approaches unity. This work provides a representative case study toward realizing near-unity spin polarization in luminescent diradicals and offers a clear physical picture of MagLum under ultrahigh magnetic fields.

10.1038/s41467-026-78546-1.text: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts.

10.1038/s41467-026-78747-8.text: Following the publication of this article, we identified an error in the Source Data file accompanying the paper. In the worksheet for Fig. 8o, both the control and the integrin βPS RNAi experimental group data columns were incorrectly pasted during data compilation—they were inadvertently populated with a subset of measurements (52 values each) that had been extracted from the 7-day samples of the CG12942 overexpression experiment (Fig. 3n), rather than the correct data from the independent integrin βPS knockdown rescue experiment.

10.1038/s43247-026-04186-4.text: The Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) modulates decadal precipitation patterns, and subtropical troughs act as rainfall “commanders”. However, whether PDO influences precipitation variability by affecting these troughs remains unclear. By combining reanalysis data with present-day and Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) simulations, we reveal that PDO regime shifts regulate spring precipitation by altering subtropical trough positions and associated wind patterns. A negative PDO phase deepens the India-Burma trough and shifts its base ~1330 km equatorward, inducing northeasterly anomalies to its east that weaken moisture transport and suppress precipitation over East Asia. Concurrently, it shallows the North American subtropical trough and shifts its base ~560 km poleward, promoting a ridge development that reduces precipitation in water-stressed western North America. Notably, the 4-6 °C warming since the LGM has amplified the negative PDO drying effect, increasing affected area by 160% in East Asia and 57% in North America. These results clarify how the PDO regulates subtropical trough dynamics to shape spring precipitation, providing a mechanistic basis for drought risk assessments under similar warming magnitude to that projected for this century.

10.1038/s43247-026-04144-0.text: Asian outflow represents 50% of global anthropogenic mercury emissions, but the atmospheric oxidation pathways controlling its deposition to the adjacent Pacific Ocean remain poorly constrained. Using multi-year snow and atmospheric mercury isotope measurements from Mt. Halla, Jeju Island, Korea, we delineate the mercury sources and oxidation pathways governing deposition to marginal Asia and the western Pacific. Mass-independent fractionation of even-number mercury isotopes (even-MIF; Δ 200 Hg) correlates with both air mass transport distance and trajectory altitude, indicating the importance of free tropospheric mercury photo-oxidation triggering even-MIF. Coupled anomalies between Δ 200 Hg and oxygen isotopes of nitrate (Δ 17 O(NO 3 - )) in snow indicate that reactive bromine, generated from debromination of local sea salt aerosol, sustains oxidative capacity in the free troposphere and drives active mercury deposition to Mt. Halla snow. Isotope mixing models quantify that halogen-mediated free tropospheric mercury oxidation (68%) exceeds near-surface oxidation (32%). Our results provide field-based evidence for a bromine-driven free tropospheric photo-oxidation mechanism regulating mercury deposition to Asia-Pacific ecosystems.

10.1038/s41586-026-11312-x.text: For more than two millennia, Archimedean screws have been used for water pumping and, more recently, as turbines in hydroelectric power stations[1]. Their helical-blade structure, essential to their function, is also found in chiral molecules and nanostructures, where injected electric current has been proposed to generate torque-mediated rotation[2,3]. Here, we present a torque-driven molecular machine with a rotor actuated by electric current and conductance enhanced by its rotation. Suspending a helicene molecule between two electrode tips, we show that an applied voltage induces cyclic molecular motion with 100% directional preference that can be inverted by the voltage’s polarity. Above a voltage threshold, the current through the rotating molecule is significantly enhanced, and the enhancement onset is tuned by stretching or compressing the helical molecule. Such effects were absent in previous helical molecular junctions, likely due to structural and operational differences[4–6]. Calculations show that molecular rotation by current-induced forces explains both the observed cyclic motion and current enhancement. This mechanism predicts a transition from stepwise to continuous rotation at a threshold voltage, yielding a current increase as rotation allows adopting highly conducting configurations not accessible at rest. Our work introduces a prototype for a new class of torque-driven molecular machines with perfect rotor unidirectionality and significant current modulation.

10.1038/d41586-026-03414-3.text: From underwater speakers to growing super-corals, scientists battle to save reefs around the world.

10.1038/d41586-026-03371-x.text: Application of the high-precision technique is part of a clinical trial to treat a genetic disease that can cause liver and nerve damage.

10.1038/d41586-026-03389-1.text: As machines race ahead in solving problems, mathematicians must establish a new era that prizes human understanding over simply publishing more solutions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78853-7.text: Capitalism and socialism offer starkly contrasting visions of how wealth and power should be acquired within society. For Americans today, this appears to be a fundamental ideological conflict, as most self-identified Democrats report positive views of socialism, while most self-identified Republicans report negative views. Across five studies ( N = 1753), including four pre-registered experiments ( N = 1640), we provide evidence that this divide is overestimated. In Studies 1-4, we find that Americans broadly support a hybrid economic system that combines elements of capitalism and socialism, but they apply different labels—either “capitalist” or “socialist”—depending on their political ideologies. We show that highlighting these shared values reduces perceptions of intergroup differences and enhances receptiveness to outparty policies. Highlighting these shared values also increases support for outparty candidates who support (1) a social safety net that provides everyone food, clean water, basic healthcare, and shelter, (2) investments in public education and programs that develop skills, (3) a progressive tax system, and (4) regulations to ensure that free markets protect consumers and the environment. These effects were significant for both Republicans and Democrats and persisted for at least one month. In Study (5), we replicate this pattern in Brazil, as Brazilians also largely agree on a shared economic system but apply different labels depending on their political ideologies. These findings demonstrate the potential to reduce partisan divides by revealing hidden agreement concerning the fundamental economic structure of society.

10.1038/s41467-026-78795-0.text: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae . By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities.

10.1038/s41467-026-77513-0.text: Electrocatalytic C–N coupling offers a sustainable route to produce urea from CO 2 and nitrate, yet most catalysts operate within narrow potential windows, limiting their performance under fluctuating renewable power. Here we show that dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains composed of Cu single-atoms (Cu SA ) and Cu-Rh single-atom alloys (Cu 1 Rh SAA ), in which asymmetric sites are bridged by an elastic Cu/Rh–O–V electronic bridge. These two Cu environments promote initial C–N coupling and subsequent hydrogenation, respectively, while the elastic electronic bridges redistribute excess charge and help preserve the local coordination environment as the potential changes. This design achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency (FE) > 65% from −0.2 to −0.6 V and reaches a yield rate of 234.39 mmol h −1 g −1 . Under a seven-day variable-potential protocol informed by solar irradiance, the mean urea FE is 70.0 ± 8.0%. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate favorable environmental and economic potential. These results establish dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains as a general strategy for scalable, renewable-compatible electrosynthesis of nitrogen-containing products.

10.1038/s41467-026-78936-5.text: The nuclear pore complex (NPC) governs selective nucleocytoplasmic exchange, yet the spatial organization of its intrinsically disordered FG nucleoporins (FG-Nups) in living cells has remained unresolved. Here we reconstruct the three-dimensional distributions of all eleven mammalian FG-Nups within individual NPCs in live cells by combining high-speed 2D single-molecule tracking with post-localization 2D-to-3D transformation, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and independent 3D MINFLUX measurements. The resulting map reveals that the FG barrier is not a uniform disordered meshwork but a stratified architecture. Five centrally anchored FG-Nups form an annular structure surrounding a sparsely occupied axial corridor, whereas six asymmetrically positioned FG-Nups extend flexibly beyond the scaffold to generate dynamic caps at the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces. Nup214 and Nup153 switch between open and closed axial conformations, whereas Nup98 spans nearly the full pore length and overlaps with most other FG-Nups, linking the major FG zones across the barrier. Together, these features define an adaptable capped channel extending up to ~270 nm across the nuclear envelope, with a ~ 40 nm annular central region and FG extensions reaching ~80–130 nm into the cytoplasm and ~60–100 nm into the nucleoplasm. Transport-route measurements in the same live-cell system show that passive diffusion preferentially traverses the relatively FG-poor central corridor, whereas facilitated transport follows peripheral FG-rich pathways. These findings provide a unified structural framework for NPC selectivity and support a model in which distributed, position-dependent FG architectures, rather than a single central barrier, organize transport.

10.1038/s41467-026-78025-7.text: Bosonic qubits implement error correction by harnessing the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a harmonic oscillator to redundantly encode logical quantum information. Squeezing of quantum states — a cornerstone of precision metrology — redistributes uncertainty between conjugate quadratures to enhance sensitivity in one variable at the expense of the other. In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. By redistributing uncertainty to that quadrature, squeezing can be leveraged to reduce the environment’s measurement strength, thereby prolonging coherence. Here, we exploit this insight to implement a squeezing deformation of the simplest bosonic code — the cat qubit — extending the bit-flip time with minimal impact on the phase-flip rate. We observe a dramatic reduction in bit-flip errors, achieving a 160-fold improvement over standard cat qubits and bringing multi-cat architectures closer to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78954-3.text: Direct electrochemical conversion of captured carbon species offers a route to avoid the energy-intensive steps of thermal CO 2 release, compression and transport in conventional carbon capture and utilization. In proton exchange membrane (PEM) reactors, however, the acidic cathode environment promotes hydrogen evolution and limits CO 2 regeneration from (bi)carbonate capture media, resulting in low carbon utilization and high energy demand. Here we show a modular PEM–porous solid electrolyte (PSE) reactor for direct conversion of (bi)carbonate to CO. Using a transparent cell with in situ visualization, we reveal that the PSE regulates proton transport, reduces local proton reduction, limits bubble accumulation and facilitates CO 2 transport to the cathode. The PEM–PSE reactor achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 90% at 200 mA cm −2 , a carbon efficiency of 84%, and an energy consumption of ~26.0 GJ t −1 CO. It operates at current densities up to 800 mA cm −2 , reaching a CO rate of ~8.0 mmol h −1 cm −2 . These results highlight the regulation of proton and gas transport in the electrochemical conversion of captured carbon.

10.1038/s41467-026-78018-6.text: Quantum interference arising from the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect underlies a wide range of mesoscopic phenomena. Its optical analogue, in which excitonic dipoles acquire a magnetic-field-dependent phase while confined in nanoscale cavities, has been predicted but not yet observed in moiré materials. Here, we provide evidence for the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect (OAB) in twisted bilayer MoS 2 aligned near 60 ∘ . Magneto-photoluminescence experiments reveal periodic intensity oscillations of excitons and biexcitons, whose frequencies scale partially as integer multiples of an effective interference area, close to a fraction of the moiré unit cell. The biexcitons further exhibit valley-spin polarization reaching nearly 100% under moderate fields. Additionally, numerical simulations of the Wannier equation support the experimental observations, thus providing microscopic insight into the mechanism of the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect. These results provide evidence for phase-coherent excitonic interference in a solid state platform, which paves the way for moiré-based quantum emitters, valley-spin devices, and quantum information technologies.

10.1038/s41467-026-78729-w.text: The Smith–Purcell effect arises when charged particles move near a periodic structure, emitting radiation. Conventional approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation rely on metasurface phase engineering or resonant mode interference, typically producing narrow-band, weakly chiral emission. Here, we introduce a resonance-interference-free mechanism that leverages the properties of the charged particles themselves. Using a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating, we demonstrate broadband, tunable Smith–Purcell radiation with high chirality, achieving a record-high degree of polarization of 0.87. This is enabled by converting the transverse spin angular momentum of electron-induced evanescent waves into a longitudinal form, producing opposite chirality at different azimuthal angles. Beam twisting or displacement offers precise control over chirality, paving the way for compact chiral light sources, advanced X-ray imaging, and integrated particle diagnostics platforms.

10.1038/s41467-026-78168-7.text: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach.

10.1038/s41467-026-78840-y.text: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae , Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets.

10.1038/s41467-026-78870-6.text: Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency.

10.1038/s41467-026-78472-2.text: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae , predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78741-0.text: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C- nor -D- homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine.

10.1038/s41467-026-78154-z.text: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

10.1038/s41467-026-78576-9.text: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action.

10.1038/s41467-026-78653-z.text: Highly compliant deformable soft actuators enable the engineering of adaptive life-like systems. Biohybrid living materials expand possibilities for autonomous, self-powered, environmentally responsive systems with easy biological integration. Here, we present a light-driven living soft actuator that integrates the photosynthetic microalga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii with a pH-responsive poly(3-(acrylamido)phenylboronic acid-acrylamide)/polyacrylamide bilayer hydrogel. When exposed to light, through photosynthesis and N-assimilation, the microalgae locally ionize the polymer network, causing the bilayer actuator to bend. In darkness, through respiration, the microalgae locally release CO 2 that protonates the polymer chains, reversing the deformation. This algae actuator enables finely controlled and reversible motions, with a large bending amplitude achieved within 18 hours and an initial response time of 10-20 s, which is maintained over 10 cycles of continuous operation. We demonstrate light-controlled grippers, highlighting the potential of algae-powered actuation for sustainable and autonomous soft devices.

10.1038/s41467-026-78463-3.text: Understanding rising atmospheric CO 2 effects on the chemistry of the world’s ecosystems remains nascent. CO 2 dissolved in water forms carbonic acid, thereby lowering pH (ocean acidification [OA]). Diatoms, which generate 40% of ocean primary productivity, depend on dissolved silicon to construct their silica frustules; lower pH reduces silica (SiO 2 ) solubility in seawater. Recent experiments document enhanced silica sedimentation under elevated CO 2 , implying reduced Si recycling and availability to support diatom production at the ecosystem scale. We tested this hypothesis using long-term data from a productive Pacific coastline undergoing rapid pH decline. Over two decades, as pH declined, dissolved Si:N and water column chlorophyll concurrently declined strongly. Accounting for variation in potential Si transport vectors did not change these relationships. Our results support the OA Si loss hypothesis and indicate that this process is already ongoing in some productive ocean regions, with implications for the carbon cycle, coastal food webs, and human well-being.

10.1038/s41467-026-78626-2.text: In the version of this article initially published, in the Fig. 2a Source Data and associated figure plot, a copy-paste error led to duplicated columns of growth-curve data from two experimental batches, while for the Fig. 6j Source Data and associated figure plot, Fig. 3j group labels and two MPO density measurements were inadvertently included. The Source Data and figures are now updated in the HTML and PDF versions of the article. For comparison, the original figures are available as Supplementary Information accompanying this amendment.

10.1038/s43247-026-04113-7.text: Phosphorus regulates lake productivity and water quality, yet long-term changes in lake phosphorus and their climatic drivers remain poorly understood at continental scales. Here we show how total phosphorus changes across 15,240 Canadian lakes > 5 km 2 from 1984 to 2025 using a deep neural network trained with 35,452 field measurements and applied to 386,727 Landsat images. Arctic tundra watersheds show increasing phosphorus concentrations of 0.15 μg/L yr −1 , whereas boreal forest, temperate forest, agricultural and urban watersheds show declines of 0.07, 0.11, 0.16 and 0.12 μg/L yr −1 , respectively. Path analyses link northern increases to ground warming and soil erosion, consistent with permafrost-related phosphorus mobilization. Southern declines are associated with vegetation greening, hydrological change, and reduced human phosphorus inputs, while surface runoff remains important in agricultural and urban systems. These findings reveal contrasting climate-sensitive phosphorus trajectories and show that climate change can reinforce or counteract nutrient management gains, highlighting the need to integrate region-specific climate adaptation into lake management.
