10.1038/s41558-026-02772-0.text: Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone (a major source of rainfall across southern Africa) can trigger devastating floods. Climate-model projections indicate that these swings might occur twice as often in the twenty-first century as in the previous century and produce more intense rainfall, owing to an increased land–sea temperature contrast and poleward intensification of atmospheric circulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78371-6.text: Supertwisted van der Waals (vdW) multilayers—in which layers are stacked with identical interlayer twist angles—enable strong and programmable chiral light–matter interactions. However, directly synthesizing these multilayers remains challenging, as the conventional growth process typically produces supertwisted spirals containing an inevitable central singularity and substantial in-plane strain. Here, we demonstrate the growth of singularity-free supertwisted WS 2 multilayers by employing a dome-shaped WS 2 monolayer as a pre-deposited template. The crack line that forms on the dome acts as a dislocation line, with its two termini serving as a conjugate pair of opposite-handed screw dislocations. This configuration enables a dislocation-guided, layer-by-layer growth process that is free of topological singularities and characterized by low residual strain. The multilayers exhibit giant chiroptical responses, including a linear-optical circular dichroism (CD) of up to 10 mdeg and a second-harmonic CD of 0.81 within an ultrathin thickness of ~ 6 nm. Our work provides an effective route for growth of supertwisted multilayers and presents a programmable platform for chiral photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w.text: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289.

10.1038/s41467-026-77770-z.text: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

10.1038/s41467-026-78517-6.text: OSTα/β is the essential basolateral transporter responsible for returning reabsorbed bile acids to the portal circulation, yet its molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human OSTα/β at 2.7 Å resolution, revealing a 7-TM architecture distinct from all established SLC transporter folds. We further determined the taurocholate (TC)-bound structure at 3.2 Å, showing that the substrate laterally binds to a surface groove on OSTα, but not in the central cavity. The TC molecule is captured by a line of conserved polar residues along the groove, which were further proved by structure-guided mutagenesis combined with transport assays. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that it is energetically favored for TC moving along the surface groove. Together, structural analysis, functional assays, and simulations demonstrate that OSTα/β mediates bile acid transmembrane translocation via a facilitated lateral diffusion mechanism with subtle conformational change, which is distinct from known SLCs. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for OSTα/β function in enterohepatic bile acid circulation and provide a foundation for therapeutic modulation of bile acid homeostasis.

10.1038/s41467-026-78827-9.text: Met1-linked ubiquitin assembled by LUBAC coordinates immune receptor signalling and inflammation. The PUB domain of the LUBAC subunit HOIP interacts with PUB-interacting motif-containing proteins, including the deubiquitinases OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Yet, how these interactions regulate LUBAC remains unclear. Here, we investigate the consequences of ablating PUB-interacting motif interactions by generating mice carrying an N101D mutation in the HOIP PUB domain. The N101D mutation causes embryonic lethality at mid-gestation driven partly by TNF receptor 1 but not solely by the loss of interaction with OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Mutation of the HOIP PUB domain causes Met1-linked autoubiquitination without inhibiting LUBAC activity, leading to superfluous Met1-linked ubiquitination of TNF receptor complex components after TNF, resulting in impaired gene activation and increased cell death. In adult mice, the N101D mutation causes cytokine storm, immune dysregulation, and weight loss. We report the HOIP PUB domain as a critical protein-interaction interface regulating LUBAC function in receptor signalling and immune homoeostasis.

10.1038/s41467-026-78899-7.text: Chagas disease (CD), caused by the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi , affects an estimated 10.5 million people worldwide and remains a leading cause of infectious cardiomyopathy in Latin America. Although infection is lifelong without treatment, only 20–30% of chronically infected individuals progress from an asymptomatic stage to clinically significant cardiac disease, and current antiparasitic therapies are limited by toxicity and variable efficacy. Reliable biomarkers capable of predicting disease progression would improve clinical risk stratification and support therapeutic development. Here, we performed a metabolomics study to identify serum biomarkers predictive of progression from asymptomatic infection to cardiac CD. Untargeted liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry profiling using complementary chromatographic platforms and univariate statistics, machine learning feature selection, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were performed to identify candidate biomarkers. These biomarkers were validated by targeted analysis. We identified eight individual metabolite biomarkers and 45 combinatorial panels predictive of progression status, including 10 panels that met sensitivity and specificity criteria defined in the target product profile for CD treatment-response biomarkers. These findings demonstrate that circulating metabolites measured at baseline can predict future cardiac disease progression and provide a foundation for clinically deployable prognostic tools in chronic Chagas disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-78781-6.text: Orthobunyaviruses, an important group of arboviruses with broad vector and host ranges, pose a persistent global public health threat, yet their cellular entry and cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. Ebinur Lake virus (EBIV), a recently identified orthobunyavirus detected in multiple countries and hosts, demonstrates potential zoonotic and spillover relevance. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2) as an entry receptor for EBIV. Knockout and ectopic expression confirm that DDR2 promotes EBIV infectivity by facilitating viral binding and internalization. The discoidin (DS) domain of DDR2 directly interacts with EBIV particles at the Gc stalk region. A soluble DS decoy or anti-DDR2 DS antibody potently inhibits EBIV infection in cell lines and primary neural cells. The DS decoy or Ddr2 knockout protects mice from lethal EBIV challenge, significantly reducing viral loads. DDR2 homologs from diverse mammals and birds bind EBIV Gc and support infection, underscoring a broad host range. Notably, we demonstrate a receptor switch among phylogenetically related orthobunyaviruses: human-infecting Germiston virus (GERV) also utilizes DDR2, while Bozo virus (BOZOV) employs DDR1. These findings establish discoidin domain receptors as functional entry receptors for orthobunyaviruses, revealing a mechanism for broad host tropism and providing insights for antiviral strategies.

10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2.text: This study quantifies drivers of water use across the food-energy-water nexus and assesses how climate change, population growth, and adaptation may reshape future water scarcity in the United States. Using high frequency water withdrawal data from 2000–2020, we disentangle the effects of climate, hydrology, and socioeconomic factors on public water use, crop irrigation, and cooling for thermoelectric power generation. Future water demands (2040–2070) are estimated using recent climate and socioeconomic projections, representing 1.0 ∘ C to 2.9 ∘ C warming and population growth ranging from 1% to 44%. Across 28 scenarios, we estimate annual water use changes ranging from -10.7% to +28.9% for public use, +32.1% to +43.6% for crop irrigation, and -27.9% to -19.9% for thermoelectric power cooling, contingent on continued adaptive efforts. Results reveal strong sectoral variation in climate sensitivity, seasonal mismatches between water supply and demand, and shifts in regional water stress under future warming.

10.1038/s41467-026-78480-2.text: Nearly one-third of global tropical cyclones (TCs) form over the western North Pacific (WNP), with severe hazards impacting Southeast and East Asia. TC genesis over the WNP underwent substantial shifts during the Cenozoic, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Tibetan Plateau uplift was crucial in shaping the present-day WNP TC genesis pattern. With the present-day land-sea configuration and sea surface temperature prescribed, Tibetan Plateau uplift from early Eocene to modern elevations accounts for nearly half of the simulated increase in TC frequency between the early Eocene and present day. Mechanistically, Tibetan Plateau uplift generates an eastward-propagating Rossby wave train, enhancing the WNP subtropical high and thereby intensifying the monsoon trough. The amplified moisture supply and reinforced upward motion within the monsoon trough collectively favor TC genesis and intensification. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of High Mountain Asia in the Cenozoic evolution of TC frequency over the WNP.

10.1038/s41467-026-75827-7.text: Brain’s structural and functional connectomes (SC and FC) offer insights into the relationship between brain circuits and cognitive functioning in people with multiple sclerosis (MS). However, diffusion and functional MRI, which are used to extract SC and FC, is expensive and time consuming, therefore are not currently used in the clinical setting. Our prior work demonstrated that estimated SC and FC (eSC and eFC) generated using MS lesion masks and artificial intelligence (AI) models can predict disability as effectively as SC and FC derived from diffusion and functional MRI in MS. In this study, we identify the eSC and eFC brain circuits that are associated with baseline and 4-year follow-up cognition and assess the ability of eSC and eFC in predicting cognition in MS. In a cohort of 171 with MS, the Network Modification tool was performed to estimate SC from the MS lesion mask, which is extracted from structural MRI scans. The eSC was then used as an input to Krakencoder, an encoder-decoder model, to estimate FC. The highest accuracy was obtained when predicting follow-up Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) using regional eSC or eFC, with a median Spearman’s correlation coefficient of 0.58 for eSC and 0.56 for eFC. Decreased eSC and eFC in the cerebellum and increased eFC in the default mode network were associated with lower follow-up SDMT scores. Our findings demonstrate that eSC and eFC derived from clinically acquired MRI and AI models can effectively predict cognition. The use of lesion-based estimates of connectomes may potentially inform clinical trials by identifying the specific brain circuits that could be targeted for the non-invasive treatments aimed at improving cognitive function in MS.

10.1038/s41467-026-78866-2.text: Metabolic reprogramming plays a critical role in heart failure (HF), but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1), a transcription factor initially identified as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, has recently been implicated in metabolic regulation. Here, we show that ZEB1 expression is reduced in failing cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Zeb1 leads to progressive HF with impaired glycolysis and fatty acid metabolism. Mechanistically, ZEB1 interacts with TEA domain transcription factor 1 (TEAD1) to activate metabolic genes, including pyruvate kinase muscle isozyme 1 (PKM1) and acetyl-CoA acyltransferase 2 (ACAA2), which regulate glycolysis and fatty acid β-oxidation, respectively. Loss of Acaa2 aggravates stress-induced cardiac hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. Acetate supplementation restores cardiac function in Zeb1 -deficient mice, whereas ZEB1 overexpression improves pressure overload- and doxorubicin-induced HF. These findings identify the ZEB1-TEAD1 axis as a regulator of cardiac metabolic homeostasis and a potential therapeutic target for HF.

10.1038/s41467-026-78819-9.text: The ion channel-forming natural product amphotericin B (AmB) can serve as a molecular prosthetic for the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) anion channel and thereby restore host defenses in cultured cystic fibrosis (CF) airway epithelia. This is despite the fact that the permeability of AmB-based channels favors cations, and these channels lose their capacity to increase airway surface liquid (ASL) pH in CF airway epithelia at high concentrations. We hypothesize that modifying such channels to favor anion permeability would increase their capacity to restore physiology in disease-relevant model systems compared to AmB. Here we show that a synthetic derivative of AmB, AmB-AA, which has an added positively charged appendage and forms ion channels with an improved relative permeability to anions, outperformed AmB in increasing the ASL pH in CF airway epithelia at both low and high concentrations. Further modifications led to another AmB derivative, C2’epiAmB-AA, that minimize cholesterol binding and thus toxicity to cultured CF airway epithelia and was an effective surrogate for CFTR in primary cultured airway epithelia from people with CF.

10.1038/s41893-026-01960-2.text: Anthropogenic emissions are rapidly increasing atmospheric CO2 levels, with severe consequences for the global climate. Researchers have developed a carbon membrane as thin as only two molecular layers that sieves and captures CO2 with very high flux and selectivity, holding promise for climate change mitigation technologies.

10.1038/s41893-026-01970-0.text: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for large-scale grid energy storage, but their widespread implementation is hindered by the lack of anolyte materials that combine high capacity, environmental compatibility, recyclability, low cost and long-term stability. While organic anolyte molecules offer a potential sustainable solution, integrating these competing attributes within a single molecular platform remains challenging. Here we report a recyclable oligo(disulfide)-based anolyte in which robust sulfur–sulfur bonds serve as redox-active sites. The anolyte is synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of potassium-form endogenous thioctic acid, providing a scalable route to high-concentration redox-active species. Paired with a sulfonated cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst, this oligo(disulfide) anolyte delivers a capacity density of 128 Ah l −1 with a 95.5% material utilization rate at 50 mA cm −2 . Using a carbon-coated sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membrane with a sulfur–sulfur bond concentration of 0.25 M, the battery retains 98.1% of its capacity over 2,200 cycles while maintaining an energy efficiency of approximately 70% at 100 mA cm −2 . We further validate the scalability and closed-loop recyclability of this chemistry in a 63 Wh stack. Our findings establish oligo(disulfide)s as a robust, circular redox platform, providing a pathway towards more resource-efficient and sustainable grid-scale energy storage.

10.1038/s41893-026-01973-x.text: As an energy-efficient and scalable alternative to conventional chemical absorption, membrane-based carbon capture requires materials that simultaneously combine molecular-level thinness, precise sub-nanometre porosity and exceptional mechanical robustness—a longstanding trilemma in separation science. Here we report graphene–amorphous carbon bilayer membranes that overcome these trade-offs by way of a graphene-guided polymer conversion approach. Leveraging a super-spreading effect, we coat graphene with a uniform, ultra-smooth, polymer-derived carbon layer as thin as 2 nm, achieving a high Young’s modulus of approximately 26.8 GPa. Controlled pyrolysis of the polymer precursor generates a carbon network featuring narrowly distributed, high-precision ultramicropores. The resulting graphene–amorphous carbon membranes exhibit sharp molecular sieving (selectivity of >60 for CO 2 /N 2 , >70 for H 2 /CO 2 and >70 for CO 2 /CH 4 ) alongside an exceptional CO 2 permeance of up to 5,000 gas permeation units that surpasses existing benchmarks. This combination of structural integrity and separation performance enables efficient carbon capture across varied flue gas, syngas and natural gas streams, establishing graphene–amorphous carbon membranes as a versatile, energy-efficient platform for sustainable molecular separations.

10.1038/s41893-026-01979-5.text: Turning water-based flow batteries into a truly sustainable technology hinges on recycling the organic molecules inside the battery. A redox-active organic molecule has now been developed that not only outperforms the industry-standard vanadium benchmark but also offers exceptional reusability.
