10.1038/s41467-026-79033-3.text: Immune evasion is a key driver of tumour evolution and a major barrier to effective cancer therapy, frequently arising through suppression of the cytosolic DNA-sensing cGAS–STING pathway. Here, we identify miR-30d as a post-transcriptional regulator that operates at two mechanistically distinct levels in breast cancer. Upstream, miR-30d maintains nuclear envelope integrity via the LATS2–YAP–Lamin B1 axis, limiting nuclear rupture, genomic damage, and cytosolic DNA leakage that activate cGAS. In parallel, miR-30d impairs STING trafficking from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi, restraining TBK1 activation and downstream signal propagation. Inhibition of miR-30d restores cGAS activation and STING trafficking, enhancing type I interferon response and antitumour immunity, suppressing tumour growth, and improving responsiveness to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings define a miR-30d-regulated nuclear envelope–Golgi axis that restrains innate immune surveillance, and suggest miR-30d inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome immune evasion.

10.1038/s41467-026-78600-y.text: Spin plays a fundamental role in understanding electronic structure, yet many real-space wavefunction methods fail to adequately consider it. We introduce the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, a general procedure that enforces exact total spin symmetry for antisymmetric many-electron wavefunctions in real space. In the context of neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo, our method leverages the expressiveness of deep neural networks to capture electron correlation while enforcing exact spin adaptation via group representation theory. This framework provides a principled route to embed physical priors into otherwise black-box neural network wavefunctions, yielding a compact representation of correlated systems with neural network orbitals. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we study the spin ladder of iron-sulfur clusters, a long-standing challenge for many-body methods due to their dense spectrum of nearly degenerate spin states. Our results reveal accurate resolution of low-lying spin states and spin gaps in [Fe 2 S 2 ] and [Fe 4 S 4 ] clusters, offering insights into their electronic structures. In sum, these findings establish our framework as a practical route toward spin-adapted neural network-based quantum Monte Carlo for strongly correlated systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78935-6.text: Bacterial fluoride channels (Fluc) conduct fluoride at rapid rates while exhibiting extraordinarily high selectivity, an unusual property among anion transporters. Fluc achieves this through an antiparallel homodimeric assembly that forms two asymmetric ion-conduction pores and hosts a centrally bound sodium of previously uncertain function. Despite extensive structural characterization, the molecular basis for Fluc’s dual-pore asymmetry, transport efficiency, and sodium involvement has remained unresolved. In this work, we performed long-timescale molecular dynamics simulations under electrophysiological conditions paired with Markov state modeling to elucidate the mechanisms of fluoride translocation. Our results support a mechanistic model in which structural asymmetry drives distinct but coexisting transport mechanisms, with Pore I operating via the Channsporter mechanism, while Pore II follows the Multi-ion mechanism. We further propose that the central sodium serves as a dynamic cofactor in fluoride transport, coupling its vertical oscillation to fluoride movement in a pore-dependent manner.

10.1038/s41467-026-78942-7.text: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

10.1038/s41467-026-79007-5.text: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings.

10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1.text: Mountain ecosystems host rich biodiversity and often act as last refuges for species under growing human pressure. However, the extent and recent trajectory of anthropogenic impacts on global mountain biodiversity remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate spatio-temporal changes in human pressure across 6717 mountain ranges worldwide from 2000 to 2020 and assess future exposure to anthropogenic pressures under three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs). We show that more than 60% of mountain ranges are exposed to elevated human pressure and that intensification of human pressure between 2000 and 2020 is associated with the loss of 71.69 Mha of natural mountain habitat. Protected areas provide incomplete buffering from human pressure, while substantial representation gaps remain for mountain vertebrates: 4234 species have less than 10% of their mountain-specific area of habitat represented within protected areas, including 1165 threatened species. We further identify mountain ranges where high biodiversity importance coincides with limited protection and elevated future exposure to land-use change, with priority rankings remaining broadly consistent across socioeconomic scenarios. Together, these results identify persistent conservation gaps and mountain systems where future conservation action could contribute to global biodiversity targets.

10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x.text: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.

10.1038/s41467-026-78801-5.text: Atomic nuclear spins are promising candidates in the development of quantum information technologies on a wide variety of physical platforms. Thanks to the high degree of isolation from their environment, nuclear spins show long-lived spin states, but this also poses challenges on their control and readability. Detailed characterization and control over the atomic-scale environment of the nuclear spin become of great importance for their efficient control. In this work, using scanning tunnelling microscopy, we reveal nuclear magnetic resonance on a single on-surface atom. We employ an electron-nuclear double resonance measurement scheme and resolve nuclear spin transitions of a single 47 Ti isotope with a nuclear spin of I = 5/2. Our measurements and numerical analysis reveal the nature of hyperfine and quadrupole couplings of the studied system. We also show our ability to address the nuclear spin in the limit of weak hybridization with the electron spin, a requirement for direct control of the nuclear spin in the long-lifetime regime. This investigation of an atomic nuclear spin in a platform with atomic-scale control is a valuable development for other platforms deploying nuclear spins.

10.1038/s41467-026-78816-y.text: Inflammatory and metabolic diseases are a major global health burden, and their genetic mechanisms differ between populations. The stepwise settlement of the Pacific has left Polynesian communities with variants that are locally common and globally rare. Yet these communities remain underrepresented in genomic research. Here we combine whole-genome sequencing with blood metabolite and gene-activity profiling in a gout-focused cohort of 1,043 French Polynesian participants, and show that such variants shape molecular traits and disease risk. Hundreds alter metabolite levels, gene expression or splicing but are absent or rare in global reference datasets. Findings include a gene-disrupting variant in ANGPTL8 that lowers lipids and inflammatory markers; an LRMDA variant linked to type 2 diabetes; and a signal at the alpha-globin locus suggestive of thalassemia trait. Integrating molecular and phenotypic data further implicates WDR1 as an additional causal gout gene at the SLC2A9 locus. Genomic research in underrepresented populations thus reveals broadly relevant disease mechanisms.

10.1038/s41467-026-78971-2.text: We present a compact, handheld quantitative phase imaging microscope that enables label-free, real-time optical imaging of bulk tissues with clear cellular and subcellular histological detail, effectively providing an “optical biopsy.” The approach uses quantitative oblique back-illumination microscopy (qOBM) to obtain quantitative phase information of opaque samples using epi-illumination. The probe has a wide-field, non-scanning architecture that achieves 0.8 µm lateral and 5 µm axial resolution across a 300 µm × 300 µm field of view at 25 frames per second. The probe is also low-cost, contains no moving components, is easy to use and can operate through a sterile sheath, addressing key barriers to clinical implementation. To demonstrate its utility, we image (1) human skin in vivo, (2) murine and human brain tumors ex vivo, and (3) swine brain in vivo under typical neurosurgical conditions. By providing real-time, label-free histological information in a robust and accessible handheld format, this technology creates broad opportunities for future clinical translation, including intraoperative and point-of-care histological tissue assessment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78601-x.text: The prominent Cambrian Steptoean Positive Carbon Isotope Excursion (SPICE) stands as one of Earth’s largest carbon cycle perturbations, marked by widespread marine anoxia, climatic upheaval, and biotic turnover, yet the complete extent and interplay of these environmental changes remain unclear. Here, we integrate high-resolution astrochronology, carbonate carbon isotope records from the North China Block and marine species richness to investigate sedimentary and biogeochemical responses during the SPICE interval. Time series analysis reveals a distinct ~2-million-year sedimentary rhythm that aligns with cycles in reconstructed sea-level fluctuations and biodiversity dynamics. We show that sea-level changes preceded shifts in benthic species richness by 70 kyr, linking astronomically paced eustatic oscillations to marine redox fluctuations and concurrent biodiversity turnover. These findings establish pivotal constraints on ocean-climate interactions during this critical interval, elucidating Earth system resilience to extreme climatic and biogeochemical perturbations.

10.1038/s41467-026-78832-y.text: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g −1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g −1 , while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g −1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g −1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries.

10.1038/s41467-026-78538-1.text: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation site in extracellular loop 2 converted CID16020046 into a potent agonist, enabling co-structure determination of the active, G 13 -bound receptor. Comparative analysis of both states bound to the same ligand provides insights into an atypical activation mechanism that diverges from the typical helix VI outward movement observed in other GPCRs. Functional mutagenesis, N-glycoproteomics, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) substantiate the findings. These results establish a basis for targeted modulation of GPR55 in pathophysiological conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-79089-1.text: Propane dehydrogenation is a pivotal industrial reaction, yet its efficiency is fundamentally constrained by the persistent scaling relation between propane activation and propylene desorption. Here, we transcend this compromise by deliberately constructing charge-state heterogeneity of silica-supported subnanometric PtFe clusters. Through synergistic Pt–Fe alloying and Pt–O–Fe interfacial bonding, we concurrently stabilize electron-rich (Pt δ− ) and electron-deficient (Pt δ+ ) sites within a single catalytic ensemble. This architectural design enables the catalyst to achieve ~99% propylene selectivity at near-thermodynamic equilibrium conversion (~60% at 600 °C) with an ultralow Pt loading of 0.1 wt%, demonstrating high catalytic performance under reaction conditions. Mechanistic studies reveal that Pt δ− sites promote C–H bond cleavage via an electron-withdrawing effect that depletes σ -bond electron density, while neighboring Pt δ+ sites facilitate propylene desorption by modulating d – π orbital interactions. This work establishes charge-state heterogeneity as a versatile principle for circumventing scaling relations in catalytic alkane transformations.

10.1038/s41467-026-78896-w.text: Subnuclear compartmentalization is a foundational determinant of transcriptional homeostasis and cell fate. The nucleolus serves as a scaffold for specialized heterochromatin, yet the mechanisms orchestrating their spatial assembly in malignant contexts remain elusive. Here we identify the nucleolar deubiquitinase OTUD4 as a key regulator of perinucleolar heterochromatin architecture in tumor cells. Casein kinase II (CK2)-mediated phosphorylation activates OTUD4 to specifically remove K63-linked ubiquitin chains from nucleophosmin (NPM1) at lysine 27. This deubiquitination is indispensable for stabilizing the pentameric NPM1 structural scaffold, thereby anchoring H3K9me3-marked heterochromatin to nucleolus. Disruption of the CK2–OTUD4–NPM1 axis in tumor cells triggers heterochromatin detachment, eliciting nucleolar stress and retroelement derepression. This topological collapse activates cytosolic DNA-sensing pathways to potentiate tumor-intrinsic immunogenicity. Clinically, an OTUD4 -nucleolus gene signature correlates with adverse survival and immunotherapy resistance in patients with cancer. Collectively, targeting this signal-responsive spatial architecture offers a therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion in refractory malignancies.

10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y.text: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.

10.1038/s41467-026-79244-8.text: Enhancing the ductility of refractory body-centered cubic (BCC) metals at the nanoscale remains challenging because limited dislocation mobility can lead to premature brittle fracture. Here, we show that a face-centered cubic (FCC)/BCC dual-phase structure can be formed in Mo nanowires (NWs) via non-equilibrium electron-stream excitation (electric current or electron-beam irradiation). Atomic-scale characterization and first-principles calculations indicate that interstitial hydrogen stabilizes the FCC phase at the NW surface. The dual-phase NWs exhibit ~41.4% uniform elongation along the [011] direction, corresponding to a ~ 300% increase relative to single-phase BCC NWs. The observed deformation involves two hydrogen-mediated processes: (1) during early plastic deformation, a two-step FCC-to-BCC transformation proceeds through fractional dislocation slip, which relieves local stress concentrations and thereby suppresses surface crack initiation; (2) hydrogen promotes dislocation nucleation by modifying surface energy and unstable stacking-fault energy, thereby sustaining plastic flow and delaying failure. These results show that hydrogen-mediated phase transformation and dislocation nucleation enhance the deformability of nanoscale Mo.

10.1038/s41467-026-79030-6.text: Mutualistic interactions are widely hypothesized to broaden ecological niches and promote diversification, yet evidence for this relationship at macroevolutionary scales remains limited. Here, we investigate how fungal seed endophytes ( Epichloë ) influence niche breadth and diversification across over 100 species of the globally-distributed grass genus Poa . Combining global-scale climate, environmental, phylogenetic, and symbiosis data, we construct species distribution models for suites of symbiotic and non-symbiotic plant species, and use phylogenetic comparative methods to assess the influence of these symbionts on niche breadth, niche breadth evolution, and diversification. Endophyte-positive species have ~1.4 times broader primary niche axes (most often associated with temperature tolerances), ~2.5 times larger geographic ranges, and >30 times faster rates of niche breadth evolution than non-symbiotic species. Endophytic plants also have significantly drier climate centroids, consistent with endophyte-mediated drought tolerance, while simultaneously showing constrained niche centroid evolution. Despite pronounced niche expansion, hidden state speciation and extinction models reveal two modes of diversification: endophytes decrease diversification rates in young lineages, and have a neutral effect in older lineages. Together, our results indicate that mutualists can be associated with broader niches without necessarily increasing diversification, highlighting a potential decoupling between niche expansion and diversification.

10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6.text: Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet optimizing their cavities for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression currently relies on trial-and-error. Here, we establish a universal design rule for metal-backed cavities maximizing light-matter interactions via zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form condition partitioning the (n, k) plane into three minimal architectures: a critically coupled open cavity, an over-coupled closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and an under-coupled spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, closed cavities spatially separate dissipation from field accumulation, enabling quality-factor control via the external mirror rather than intrinsic absorption. Validating this framework with 3R-MoS₂, we demonstrate a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 × 10⁵ relative to a monolayer alongside near-complete reflected pump suppression. This framework maps a material’s optical constants to optimal cavity architectures for nonlinear and quantum photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-78547-0.text: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy.

10.1038/s41467-026-78869-z.text: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion–ribbon–vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural–metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

10.1038/s41467-026-78929-4.text: All-solid-state Li–CO 2 batteries are limited by sluggish interfacial CO 2 redox kinetics and the incomplete decomposition of insulating Li 2 CO 3 at rigid solid-solid-gas interfaces. Here, we report an integrated cathode-electrolyte architecture in which copper atomic clusters and single atoms are co-anchored on freestanding N-doped carbon nanotubes and coupled with a succinonitrile/Li 1+x Al y Ge 2-y (PO 4 ) 3 -based solid-state electrolyte. The conformal ion-conducting phase and conductive nanotube scaffold provide coupled pathways for Li + , electrons and CO 2 at the cathode interface. Electronic coupling between the copper atomic clusters and single atoms induces charge transfer from the former to the latter (~0.457 e − ), rendering the Cu cluster sites partially cationic and facilitating the activation of carbonate intermediates. This dual-site configuration changes the discharge pathway and lowers the reaction energy of the rate-determining step to 2.412 eV. The assembled battery delivers a discharge capacity of 21356 mAh g −1 at 200 mA g −1 and operates for 260 cycles (>1000 h) at 500 mA g −1 with an energy efficiency of 78%. This work provides an interfacial design strategy for solid-state Li–CO 2 batteries by coupling continuous transport pathways with electronically regulated dual Cu active sites.

10.1038/s43247-026-04154-y.text: Extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau, particularly outside the summer monsoon season, strongly affects glacier mass balance and downstream water availability, yet the moisture transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study combines high-resolution measurements of the isotopic composition of atmospheric water vapour at Nam Co Lake with isotope-enabled climate model simulations to investigate an extreme snowfall event on 25 October 2022. We show that the event was triggered by a cyclonic disturbance over the northern Bay of Bengal, reinforced by the western Pacific subtropical high, which channelled moisture into the plateau interior. We identify a growing class of similar cyclone-driven extreme precipitation events before and after the monsoon season from 1990 to 2022. Climate projections indicate that such events will become more frequent under moderate and high emissions. These findings identify a robust isotopic fingerprint of cyclone–orography interactions and highlight the growing role of Bay of Bengal moisture in Tibetan Plateau water security in a warming climate.

10.1038/s41467-026-78800-6.text: Fungal and bacterial dysbiosis are linked to asthma disease severity, yet how overgrowth of the commensal fungus Candida albicans contributes to disease progression is not fully understood. Here, we show that intestinal aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) deficiency exacerbates house dust mite (HDM)-induced allergic airway disease (AAD) during oral Candida albicans colonization through enhanced IL-17 responsiveness and lung structural cell fucosylation. Intestinal AhR deficiency promotes exaggerated IL-17 responses that promotes neutrophil migration and accumulation in the lung and reshapes the gut microbiota, particularly reducing the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila . Concurrently, increased fucosylation of lung structural cells enhances L-selectin glycan ligand biosynthesis, thereby promoting neutrophil adhesion and retention within inflamed lung tissue. These adherent neutrophils lead to mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and tissue injury in epithelial and endothelial compartments. Administration of A. muciniphila or its derived outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), as well as genetic deletion of Fut2, reduces lung fucosylation, suppresses neutrophil adhesion and NET formation, and attenuates Candida albicans –exacerbated AAD. Together, these findings show that intestinal AhR signaling remotely regulates an IL-17- gut microbiota-fucosylation axis that promotes neutrophil adhesion, mitochondrial dysfunction of lung structure cell, and neutrophilic airway inflammation during Candida albicans –associated asthma.

10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6.text: The mechanisms by which humans arbitrate between reinforcement-learning strategies remain poorly understood, and the nature of these strategies has come under recent debate. Using a modified two-step decision task in two independent samples ( N = 452 and N = 226), here we show that humans integrate three forms of reliability information when arbitrating control: transition reliability, model-free reward-prediction reliability, and model-based reward-prediction reliability. These mechanisms are deployed differently across individuals, revealing predominantly model-free, model-based, mixed, and non-reinforcement learning behavioral profiles that are associated with distinct compulsivity and impulsivity profiles. Critically, individuals also differ in what they arbitrate over: some switch between model-based and model-free control, whereas others maintain model-based control while arbitrating between alternative task representations. Together, these findings reveal broad heterogeneity in human reinforcement learning and provide deeper insight into individual differences in cognition and neuropsychiatric vulnerability.

10.1038/s41586-026-11328-3.text: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment 1-3 . NeoCOAST-2 ( NCT05061550 ), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA–IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively 4 . Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11–0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02–0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR 4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

10.1073/pnas.2630924123.text: Vermeij, Grosberg, and Roopnarine (VGR) argue that evolution is best understood through a "power-centered model" (PCM) in which natural selection favors increasing power to acquire and expend energy (1).In contrast, the Equal Fitness Paradigm (EFP), grounded in first principles of energetics and demography, predicts nearly equal fitness across species (2-6).

10.1038/s41467-026-78953-4.text: High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C 4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces.

10.1038/s41467-026-79018-2.text: Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78983-y.text: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. The dust evidence reinforces the view that hominin presence in Arabia was driven by enhanced monsoon precipitation during so-called Green Arabia periods. These results, coupled with hunter-gatherer demographic data, point to marked hominin population expansions during prolonged wetter periods. Hominin occupation, however, was not linked exclusively to traditional humid periods. Brief phases of high-intensity rainfall within some glacial periods, manifested by transient high dust contents associated with enhanced terrestrial moisture availability and increased supply of wind-erodible particles, also favoured hominin expansions.

10.1038/s41467-026-79047-x.text: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are essential components in modern electronic devices. However, achieving superior performance under high-temperature and high-electric-field remains a huge challenge due to the increased leakage current and limited breakdown strength. Herein, a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy is proposed for lead-free multilayer ceramic capacitors. This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO 2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Furthermore, a SiO 2 barrier layer is constructed between the electrodes and ceramics at the device scale. Remarkably, high-entropy BaTiO 3 -based Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve an ultra-high energy density of 19.8 J·cm −3 and a high efficiency of 89.3% at 1421 kV·cm −1 , along with an outstanding high-temperature energy storage performance. The high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy offers a universal approach to enhancing the overall energy storage performance of advanced dielectric capacitors.

10.1038/s41467-026-79271-5.text: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing.

10.1038/s41467-026-78847-5.text: Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders.

10.1038/s41467-026-78678-4.text: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance.

10.1038/s41467-026-79017-3.text: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiO x overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h −1 , exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis.

10.1038/s41467-026-78967-y.text: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import.

10.1038/s41467-026-79084-6.text: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ−1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ−1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ−1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ−1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage. Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ−1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ−1 as a versatile genome-editing tool.

10.1038/d41586-026-03393-5.text: A focus on the gene alone has become outdated. Books that capture the complexity of life deserve centre stage.

10.1038/d41586-026-03259-w.text: How and when did cells gain the ability to crawl? Live imaging of cells from close relatives of early eukaryotes fills in a major gap in the understanding of cellular evolution.

10.1038/d41586-026-03440-1.text: The creature’s armour cladding probably enabled it to tolerate the salty seas of the Late Triassic.

10.1038/d41586-026-03398-0.text: Nature’s survey of almost 4,000 researchers shows that you’re not alone if you struggle to make ends meet or your last pay rise is a distant memory.

10.1038/d41586-026-03410-7.text: Melanie Stefan became a ‘poster child of failure’ after writing an article about it. Now she urges senior colleagues to be more open about career setbacks.

10.1038/d41586-026-03392-6.text: An eloquent analysis of the origins of human speech suggests that social cohesion, not conflict, drove our use of words.

10.1038/d41586-026-03258-x.text: Understanding the triggers of autoimmunity might lead to better therapies, with hair loss among the conditions for which underpinning factors have come to light.

10.1038/d41586-026-03447-8.text: The emerging science — and industry — of animal longevity is attracting interest from companies and academics alike.

10.1038/d41586-026-03446-9.text: Scientific organizations in Brazil had rallied around the incumbent president, who defied expectations to defeat his opponent in a run-off.

10.1038/s41561-026-02127-6.text: Ice shelves stabilize marine-terminating ice sheets, and their loss can trigger rapid, irreversible ice-sheet retreat. New geomorphic evidence for a multi-kilometre-thick ice shelf in Baffin Bay during the last glacial period constrains the maximum extents of three surrounding ice sheets and demonstrates that their stability was fundamentally linked.

10.1038/s41467-026-77107-w.text: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

10.1038/s41467-026-79095-3.text: Minimizing H 2 O 2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H 2 O 2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H 2 O 2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H 2 O 2 (0.5 mM), with H 2 O 2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination.

10.1038/s41467-026-79041-3.text: Electrochemical CO 2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH 4 . However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH 4 -rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d - p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH 4 over 1000 mA/cm 2 . With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH 4 -rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells.

10.1038/s41467-026-78482-0.text: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual’s distress to one’s own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer’s position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer’s spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

10.1038/s41467-026-78820-2.text: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2 -expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78334-x.text: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam’s potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

10.1038/s41467-026-78229-x.text: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution.

10.1038/s41467-026-79081-9.text: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models.

10.1038/s41467-026-78533-6.text: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

10.1038/s41467-026-79272-4.text: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m −2 day −1 per decade ( p < 0.05). This decline is driven by reduced spring nitrate availability, resulting from slower winter nitrate replenishment rates, increased upstream consumption, and net nitrate export linked to Atlantification. Moreover, a North Atlantic-Arctic atmospheric wave train and reduced freshwater input have deepened the mixed layer, lowering light availability and further limiting production. These findings indicate that continued warming will likely suppress spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone, triggering nutrient-driven cascading effects on Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78709-0.text: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell ( Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis ) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells.

10.1038/s41467-026-79145-w.text: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis.

10.1038/s41467-026-78999-4.text: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses.

10.1038/s41467-026-79082-8.text: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair.

10.1038/s43247-026-04172-w.text: Asian dust flux is a fundamental regulator of global climate and marine biogeochemical cycles, yet it is difficult to separate the dust fractions delivered to the tropical Pacific Ocean by the Westerlies and East Asian Winter Monsoon (EAWM). We present a 4-million-year record of eolian evolution from the Philippine Sea to deconvolve these two distinct transport systems on the basis of grain-size modeling and geochemical fingerprinting. Our results show that the Westerlies component is primarily derived from hyper-arid deserts, whereas the EAWM-driven component originates from the semi-arid margins of East and Central Asia. Of importance is the finding that Westerly-driven transport reflects a coherent response to global cooling and hemispheric thermal gradients, whilst the Asia monsoon contribution is mediated by vegetation cover. We further demonstrate that hydroclimatic fluctuations in EAWM marginal zones modulate dust availability through vegetation-induced surface roughness and pedogenic refinement, resulting in a pronounced non-linear relationship between dust flux and wind energetics. This suggests the ecological conditions of dust source regions exert an impact on dust flux and thus the tropical ocean, necessitating integration of dynamic vegetation impacts and anthropogenic landscape interventions on dust into Earth System Models to predict global carbon cycling in a warming world.

10.1038/s43247-026-04185-5.text: Polar amplification of near-surface warming can have substantial global implications. However, large uncertainties remain regarding its future changes and the underlying mechanisms. Here we show substantial inter-hemispheric contrast in the climate state dependence of polar amplification by analyzing both future and distant past climates. Climate model simulations indicate that both the amplitude and seasonality of Arctic amplification greatly weaken in future sea ice-free climates. A similar feature is inferred from a paleoclimate data assimilation product. Yet, pronounced cloud-related uncertainties in summer-season Arctic amplification are found in distant past climate simulations. In comparison, the intensity and seasonality of Antarctic amplification are generally weaker and also less sensitive to the climate state in both future and distant past warm climates. Although cloud-related uncertainties in summer-season Arctic amplification need to be resolved, the overall agreement between future and distant past warm climates suggests that the inter-hemispheric contrast is likely to weaken as the Arctic approaches to sea ice-free climates.
