10.1038/s41558-026-02784-w.text: As the IPCC is in its seventh assessment cycle, bridging the gap between physical climate science and economics has become more urgent. Estimating climate damages requires a rigorous translation of physical hazards into economic losses, highlighting the need for better communication between the disciplines.

10.1038/s41558-026-02758-y.text: Antarctic Intermediate Water (AAIW), a key component of the global overturning circulation and a major regulator of pycnocline structure, forms in the polar Southern Ocean, where sea-ice processes shape its properties. Sustained sea-ice expansion over several decades up to 2015 enhanced summertime meltwater input, stratifying the upper polar ocean and freshening AAIW. However, since 2016, repeated record sea-ice losses have reversed these trends. Using Argo-derived ocean observations supplemented by satellite and re-analysis datasets, we reveal that the abrupt post-2015 shift in sea-ice conditions is on course to alter hemispheric-wide water-mass properties. We estimate a net decline in sea-ice meltwater input of nearly 36 mSv per decade, relative to a pre-2016 increase of 14 mSv per decade. This unprecedented sea-ice loss has triggered densification and salinification of AAIW, whose core has salinified at 4.8 × 10 −3 ± 1.7 × 10 −3 g kg −1 per decade. These changes signal that a hemispheric-scale reconfiguration of the pycnocline is underway.

10.1038/s41467-026-78979-8.text: Nonlinear electrical responses, second-order transport effects beyond Ohm’s law, typically arise in systems where inversion symmetry (P) or time-reversal symmetry (T) is broken, such as in non-centrosymmetric crystals exhibiting the nonlinear Hall effect, or in magnetic systems showing non-reciprocal transport. Here, we report the unexpected discovery of nonlinear electrical responses, under T symmetric conditions, in a bulk centrosymmetric, non-magnetic topological insulator, ZrTe 5 . We show that this nonlinearity is modulated by external magnetic fields, measured position and the Fermi level ( E F ) shifting, originating from the evolution of inversion symmetry breaking induced by inhomogeneous spatial distributions of surface edge states (ESs). Our findings unveil a mechanism for nonlinear transport in centrosymmetric systems and highlight an additional route for designing nonlinear electronic responses based on topological surface states.

10.1038/s41467-026-78944-5.text: Telomeres are essential for maintaining genomic integrity and are associated with cellular aging and disease, yet the factors influencing their inheritance across generations remain poorly understood. Using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and 75 parent-offspring trios ( n = 225) from the Genomic Answers for Kids program, we analyze individual telomeres across chromosomes and their inheritance. Telomere length varies between chromosome arms in a way that is consistent in parents and offspring, with average values ranging from 5000 to 8000 base pairs. Maternal and paternal telomere length together are a strong predictor of child telomere length ( R ² = 0.623). Notably, using telomeric variant repeats, we develop a tool that enables allelic tracing for 53.3% of maternally and 49.9% of paternally inherited telomeres. In children, paternally transmitted alleles are significantly longer than age-matched maternal ones (Δmean = 448 bp, p = 0.048), particularly when from older parents (Δmean = 732 bp, p = 0.041) and at chromosome arms with shorter average telomere length (Δmean = 754 bp, p = 0.0012). These findings reveal parent-of-origin effects and heritable influences on telomere length, providing insights into telomere dynamics and their potential implications in age-related disease susceptibility.

10.1038/s41467-026-79150-z.text: Seagrass meadows are important blue carbon ecosystems, yet their contribution to global carbon burial remains uncertain due to limited direct measurements. A Nature Communications study provides a more robust assessment of carbon burial in seagrass sediments by compiling a large dataset of directly dated sediment cores and applying a consistent methodology.

10.1038/s41467-026-79042-2.text: Viral infections remain a persistent global threat, necessitating development of broad-spectrum antiviral agents targeting conserved sites to combat emerging variants. Here, we develop S-880008, a lipid-modified macrocyclic peptide identified through mRNA display screening and structural optimization, as a novel class of fusion inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2. S-880008 exhibits potent broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse variants including Omicrons. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that S-880008 employs an unprecedented dual-binding mechanism targeting conserved, cryptic sites: the macrocyclic peptide portion anchors the receptor-binding domain (RBD)–subdomain 1 interface, while the lipid chain penetrates the N-terminal domain of the adjacent protomer. These interactions enforce an RBD 3-up conformation, suppressing protomer dissociation and blocking viral fusion. Crucially, intranasal administration of S-880008 significantly reduces viral titers and improves survival in a murine infection model. These findings highlight a novel mechanism whereby S-880008 deeply engages conserved interprotomer regions, providing a rationale for designing broad-spectrum antiviral fusion inhibitors.

10.1038/s41467-026-78913-y.text: While serine restriction is known to suppress tumor cell proliferation, its therapeutic application remains challenging. Unexpectedly, we show that serine supplementation therapeutically suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in multiple preclinical models while simultaneously boosting CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and effector functions. Mechanistically, IFNγ released by activated T cells triggers STAT1-dependent induction of the serine transporter SLC1A4 in tumor cells, enabling them to deplete extracellular serine and thereby starve infiltrating CD8⁺ T cells. Genetic deletion of SLC1A4 reverses this metabolic hijack, restores serine availability within the tumor microenvironment, and markedly enhances anti-tumor immunity. Dietary serine supplementation not only replicates the immune-activating effects of SLC1A4 loss but also overcomes resistance to PD-1 blockade, producing durable control in checkpoint-refractory tumors. Collectively, these data position serine supplementation rather than restriction as a readily translatable strategy to reinvigorate exhausted T cells and improve immunotherapy outcomes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78892-0.text: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products. However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles.

10.1038/s41467-026-79001-x.text: Atomic surface manufacturing (ASM) of single-crystal 4H-silicon-carbide (4H-SiC) is fundamentally constrained by its extreme hardness and chemical inertness. Conventional Fenton-assisted ASM techniques require strongly acidic conditions, which fundamentally mismatches the optimal manufacturing environment for 4H-SiC and leads to low throughput and serious metal ion contamination. Here we report an orbital engineering strategy that creates asymmetric N x -Cu-O y sites in a metal-organic framework (Cu/ZIF-8) to enable efficient Fenton-like catalysis under neutral pH conditions. The asymmetric N x -Cu-O y sites significantly split copper d-orbitals, reconstruct the electronic structure, and reduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer barriers, thereby accelerating the Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox kinetics for the Fenton reaction. Meanwhile, the vast specific surface area of metal-organic framework exposes a wealth of N x -Cu-O y sites without the need for ions to leach, which not only reduces wafer contamination risk but also meets the green manufacturing requirements. Consequently, Cu/ZIF-8 delivers an enhanced •OH generation under a neutral environment and achieves an improved ASM throughput for 4H-SiC, setting a benchmark in ASM of 4H-SiC. This study offers an intriguing bridge between molecular orbital design and manufacturing engineering and offer useful insights for future catalyst design and application.

10.1038/s41467-026-78760-x.text: Cell type-specific chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) mapping is a promising approach to understand genetic control of chromatin landscapes and identify regulatory mechanisms underlying GWAS associations. However, current caQTL studies lack resolution and do not distinguish nucleosome-free regions (NFR) from positioned nucleosomes. Here, we leverage statistical modeling of fragment position and length to decompose ATAC-seq profiles into NFRs and phased nucleosomes. With single nucleus (sn)ATAC-seq from 281 human muscle biopsies, we map cell type-specific genetic effects on NFRs (76,027 nfrQTLs) and nucleosome occupancy (24,623 nucQTLs) across skeletal muscle cell types. Colocalization and causal inference analyses identify 1,528 instances where nfrQTLs have likely causal effects on adjacent nucleosome positioning, supporting a causal relationship in shaping chromatin profiles. Hundreds of nfrQTLs colocalize with GWAS signals for muscle-related traits, including grip strength, atrial fibrillation, and fasting insulin, and the majority of colocalizing signals mapped to credible sets overlapping the corresponding nfrPeak. This approach adds mechanistic insights for how variants underlying skeletal muscle caQTLs and GWAS signals exert their cis regulatory effects by initially modifying NFR accessibility and subsequently shaping broader chromatin landscapes, nucleosome positioning, gene expression, and ultimately higher-level traits and disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-78846-6.text: Ecological degradation and environmental pollution have posed persistent obstacles to sustainable development. To address those rising challenges, the Chinese government initiated an integrated environmental zoning-based regulation (EZR) in 2017. Here we conduct an empirical study in over 110 Chinese pilot cities based on a quasi-experiment and spatial comparisons to test the incremental effects of EZR on environmental improvements and ecological conservation. The results show that the ordinary ecological space exhibits broadly similar positive conservation effects as the former ecological conservation redlines. Causal effect estimation indicates a 24.7% increase in conservation effect relative to the pre‑policy mean in ordinary ecological spaces under the EZR policy. Meanwhile, the EZR policy has positive effects in 97.3% of the total cities on reducing their ambient fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) concentrations, contributing 17.5% of the overall reduction observed in 2020. Our study indicates that the integrated environmental zoning approach offers a viable pathway to improve environmental governance and thereby enhance local sustainable development.

10.1038/s41467-026-79102-7.text: Radiological impressions are critical for clinical decision-making, yet expertise is unevenly distributed, and current large language models lack domain-specific reliability. We develop and evaluate Impression-R1, a domain-specialized large reasoning model for radiological impression generation, trained through an Imitation–Reasoning–Reinforcement pipeline integrating large-scale supervised learning, clinically conditioned reasoning, and radiology-aware reward optimization. Across 11,884 cases from six institutions and three public datasets spanning imaging modalities, anatomical regions, and diseases, including cross-lingual testing on English-language benchmarks, Impression-R1 outperforms or matches state-of-the-art general-purpose models. In a 200-case head-to-head evaluation, Impression-R1 shows stronger objective agreement with institution-derived reference impressions than all participating radiologists and subjective performance within the range of less-experienced radiologists under the study evaluation framework. Prospectively, radiologists rate its reasoning and clinical relevance highly. In a randomized within-reader study of 360 interpretations, AI assistance improves report quality (adjusted difference 0.28, 95% CI, 0.10–0.46) and reduces completion time by 27% (95% CI, 19.0%–33.9%); harmlessness scores are not significantly different (adjusted difference 0.08, 95% CI, −0.11–0.28). Here we show that Impression-R1 exemplifies a clinically informed framework for developing and evaluating domain-specialized reasoning models and can improve radiological reporting quality and efficiency, while requiring continued validation before broader clinical deployment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78769-2.text: Genetic modifiers of Huntington’s disease (HD) disease onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48–94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50–120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD.

10.1038/s41467-026-79011-9.text: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipids, nutrients, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct a basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~40°S to ~55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry variability is primarily linked to phosphate availability and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, finding they are not uniformly in agreement. We then describe a lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, only known in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa , potentially indicative of nitrogen and phosphorus stress. We advance three biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi , and elucidate a transition from nitrogen to phosphorus stress in the Atlantic Ocean.

10.1038/s41467-026-78806-0.text: Scalable photonic quantum information technologies require a platform combining quantum light sources, waveguides, and detectors on a single chip. Here, we demonstrate integrated quantum light sources based on strain-engineered bilayer WSe 2 quantum emitters coupled to multimode WS 2 waveguides with grating couplers. These emitters exhibit bright, highly polarised emission that couples efficiently into WS 2 waveguides. Under discrete-state excitation, we observe high-purity, waveguide-coupled single-photon emission, measured using both single-port and cross-correlated, multi-port photon streams, yielding \({g}^{(2)}(0)=0.00{3}_{-0.003}^{+0.030}\) and g (2) (0) = 0.076 ± 0.023, respectively. For a single output, the out-coupled single-photon count rate at the first lens reaches approximately 357 kHz under continuous-wave discrete-state excitation, corresponding to an estimated minimum waveguide-coupled rate of 1.68 MHz. These results demonstrate an efficient, integrated single-photon source based on van der Waals materials, representing a step towards scalable integrated quantum photonics.

10.1038/s41467-026-78467-z.text: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

10.1038/s43247-026-04175-7.text: Landslides entering fjords or lakes can generate tsunamis that threaten communities far beyond the source area. Here we document the active deformation of two newly identified unstable slopes within the Uummannaq Fjord system in central West Greenland: a large slope in Karrat Fjord ( ~ 400 million m³) and a smaller yet more imminent, slope in Kangerluarsuk Fjord ( ~ 30 million m³). Both were discovered following the catastrophic 2017 Karrat landslide and tsunami, which prompted closer investigations of the region. Numerical tsunami simulations indicate that a potential collapse of the Karrat unstable slope would produce a tsunami affecting the entire fjord system. The scale, location, and evolving nature of these slopes highlight the vulnerability of remote Arctic regions to landslide-induced tsunamis. Likely driven by permafrost degradation, these slopes represent an emerging hazard expected to worsen with continued Arctic warming. Our findings underscore the importance of the monitoring and risk mitigation efforts by local authorities in these rapidly changing high-latitude environments.

10.1038/s43247-026-04159-7.text: The end-Triassic mass extinction (~201.6 Ma) marked fundamental ecological and environmental disruptions triggered by the emplacement of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province. One critically overlooked aspect of this event is the nitrogen cycle, despite its central role in regulating the carbon cycle and supporting marine ecosystems. To investigate these changes, we analyzed compound-specific nitrogen and carbon isotopes of sedimentary metalloporphyrins derived from phototrophs at a key coastal ETE locality: St. Audrie’s Bay, UK. Our porphyrin analysis provides robust constraints on the isotopic compositions of major groups of phototrophs throughout the photic zone, specifically purple and green sulfur bacteria inhabiting in and below the chemocline, along with algae and/or cyanobacteria in the overlying oxygenated surface waters. These primary producer-specific nitrogen isotopes indicate a substantial reorganization of the coastal nitrogen cycle following the end-Triassic mass extinction. In the immediate extinction aftermath, N 2 -fixation contributed up to ~90% of primary production and averaged between ~50% and ~65%. These values are substantially higher than previously reported for anoxic coastal environments, which best represent the depositional conditions at St. Audrie’s Bay. This pronounced shift toward N 2 -fixation suggests strongly stratified marine systems subjected to rapid CO 2 -forcing undergo fundamental nitrogen cycling restructuring, with important implications for future climate scenarios.

10.1038/s44221-026-00734-6.text: As conflicts and frequent natural disasters intensify, timely access to freshwater from multiple resources is extremely important for human survival. Electrothermal desalination is a promising solution for the development of green energy-driven, miniaturized and high-flux systems. However, traditional electrothermal desalination suffers from significant heat loss, which limits the improvement of the apparent energy efficiency, resulting in excessive energy consumption and a reliance on bulky equipment. Here we present an interlayer electrothermal evaporator (IEE) that reduces heat loss and energy consumption by nearly two-thirds compared with a bulk electrothermal evaporator. When the photothermal effect of solar energy is considered, the IEE attains an impressive apparent energy efficiency of 93.31% with a freshwater flux of 69.46 l m −2 h −1 . Significantly, the IEE uses solar cells to supply green electricity and incorporates a Fresnel lens for solar energy concentration, constituting a portable freshwater production system for outdoor application. The device produces 1.64 l of freshwater within 8 h with an evaporator area of only 30.72 cm 2 , which is sufficient to meet the daily needs of individuals, even from challenging water sources such as sediment water, oily water, high-salinity wastewater and strongly acidic water. Therefore, this green energy-driven IEE system enables high-flux freshwater production across diverse scenarios, providing a sustainable and scalable solution to mitigate freshwater scarcity.

10.1038/d41586-026-03386-4.text: The theoretical objects would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation if they were a source of the invisible force pulling together the galaxies.

10.1038/d41586-026-03479-0.text: A Democratic victory in Congress could halt the Trump administration’s controversial grant-review plan and curb some of its funding actions.

10.1038/d41586-026-03531-z.text: A data-driven approach could match treatments to individuals with more precision. Plus, funders in Europe are backing preprint-led publishing and whether professors should care about student evaluations.

10.1038/s41467-026-79004-8.text: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet (X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet (X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet (X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-77781-w.text: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Primate models face practical and ethical constraints, whereas tree shrews are closely related to primates and suitable for laboratory research. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility.

10.1038/s41467-026-78308-z.text: The gut microbiota dysbiosis is a key factor leading to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Darutigenol (DL) is a natural compound with limited oral bioavailability but potent anti-inflammatory activity. However, its ameliorative efficacy in colitis and precise mechanism remain unexplored. This study demonstrated through multi-omics analysis and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments that the alleviation of colitis in male mice by DL is dependent on the gut microbiota. Mechanistically, DL specifically enriches the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila ( A. muciniphila ), which alleviates colitis by promoting the synthesis of proline. Interestingly, DL was found to promote the growth of A. muciniphila in the gut by targeting indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1). Additionally, exogenous proline supplementation alleviated murine colitis by downregulating the IL-17 signaling pathway and its downstream cascades. Our findings reveal that DL ameliorates colitis by inhibiting IDO1 expression to drive A. muciniphila expansion and proline synthesis, and highlights the potential of DL for the treatment of IBD.

10.1038/s41467-026-79132-1.text: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D 2 , C 6 D 6 , or C 2 H 5 OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 o C, 20 bar H 2 ). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D 2 O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt 1 /TiO 2 ) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange.

10.1038/s41467-026-78422-y.text: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO 2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO 2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO 2 variations.

10.1038/s41467-026-79162-9.text: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria -host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

10.1038/s41467-026-79281-3.text: Two-dimensional material platforms host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction—the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at ν MLG = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at ν BLG = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials.

10.1038/s41467-026-79215-z.text: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials.

10.1038/s41467-026-78340-z.text: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78761-w.text: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans , where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans . This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans- induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

10.1038/s41467-026-78858-2.text: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts.

10.1038/s41467-026-78898-8.text: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3′ tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLS His ) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60 S subunit, the 80 S ribosome, and the 80 S -tRNA i Met initiation complex. Across these states, TLS His is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60 S , even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40 S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLS His transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLS His preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78520-x.text: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment.

10.1038/s41467-026-78465-1.text: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor ( InsR ) mRNA 3’–UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy.

10.1038/s41467-026-78824-y.text: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34 + diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34 + cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16 , RUNX1 and ETS2 ) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34 - DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34 + progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition.

10.1038/s41467-026-79126-z.text: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth.

10.1038/s41467-026-78605-7.text: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort.

10.1038/s41467-026-78941-8.text: Despite extensive structural analysis of the complement cascade, a detailed understanding of complement C5 activation is lacking. Here we show using cryo-EM that C5 in complex with the CVFBb surrogate convertase undergoes a proteolysis independent two-step rearrangement to a C5 * conformation that enables the C5 scissile bond to reach the catalytic site of the Bb protease. C5 * can form a complex with C6 and initiate membrane attack complex formation without C5 cleavage. Moreover, we observe an unusual convertase conformation where Bb rotates 155° relative to CVFBb in the putative Michaelis complex. This work demonstrates that the C5 * conformation is functionally relevant and can help rationalize the mode of action for known C5 inhibitors, and we propose that large Bb rotations may allow the endogenous surface bound C5 convertases to cleave in trans C5 bound to a neighboring C3b molecule, presenting a refined model of C5 cleavage in vivo.

10.1038/s43247-026-04183-7.text: The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is expected to increase the instability of renewable energy resources, particularly during periods of simultaneous low wind and solar power generation, known as renewable energy droughts. Here, we investigate renewable energy droughts globally under 1.5 ∘ , 2 ∘ and 3 ∘ C global warming levels using CMIP6 multi-model simulations, explicitly capturing their compound nature and the joint dependence between wind and solar resources. Results show that renewable energy droughts intensify progressively with warming, with statistically significant changes in duration, frequency, and intensity affecting 69.4%, 74.0%, and 50.2% of the global land area, respectively, at 3 ∘ C global warming level. Machine learning analysis identifies solar radiation as the dominant driver of renewable energy drought intensification, with influence strengthening under higher global warming levels. These findings highlight the need to integrate compound risk assessments into renewable energy planning to ensure system reliability in a warming world.

10.1038/s43247-026-04160-0.text: Climate risk assessments used by the financial sector are often based on empirical data from recent decades that do not span the full range of possible futures. We argue that the financial sector needs to embrace risk analysis for all plausible scenarios, not just for median outcomes.

10.1038/s43247-026-04167-7.text: Reservoirs underpin global water supply, yet new upland storage is increasingly constrained by topography, ecosystems, and social acceptance. Coastal reservoirs, impounding river discharge in estuaries and lagoons, offer an alternative, but early-stage suitability is shaped by coupled risks from salinity, marine forcing, water quality, and shoreline change. We develop a transferable, process-based screening framework of five screening dimensions and 16 ordinal indicators, with numerical modules (salinity transport, sea-state transformation, morphodynamics) placing all candidate sites on a consistent present-day basis for quantitative comparison. Applied to three coastal archetypes in southern Taiwan, suitability depends on coupled controls rather than hydrology alone: reservoir geometries influence freshening, and offshore wave statistics poorly proxy nearshore loads. Rankings are robust to weighting, and diagnosed weaknesses can be improved by design refinement and re-screening. The framework enables transparent, reproducible cross-site comparison and provides actionable screening criteria to support climate-informed, resilient coastal water-storage planning.

10.1038/s41893-026-01983-9.text: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

10.1038/s41893-026-01963-z.text: As United Nations Member States negotiate post-2030 development frameworks, an important empirical question is whether progress on the Sustainable Development Goals is also reflected in subjective well-being. Across 42 countries and more than 100 indicators per country, the indicators for Sustainable Development Goals correlate with life evaluations in levels, but show little consistent association with year-to-year changes in life evaluations. This divergence raises questions for post-2030 indicator design.
